chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab from Mu'mmar ibn Khallad, who said to me: Ar-Rayyan ibn al-Salt said

in Marv, and Al-Fadl ibn Sahl had sent him to some of the districts of Khorasan. He said to me: 'I would like you to seek permission for me to enter upon Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), so that I may greet him. And I would like him to clothe me from his garments and to gift me from the dirhams that were minted in his name.' So I entered upon Ar-Rida (peace be upon him), and he began by saying to me: 'Indeed, Ar-Rayyan ibn al-Salt wishes to enter upon us, and to receive clothing from our garments and a gift from our dirhams.' So I granted him permission, and he entered and greeted. Then the Imam gave him two garments and thirty dirhams from the dirhams minted in his name.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan, a title for Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.)
key_terms.الرَّيَّانُ بْنُ الصَّلْتِ: Ar-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, a prominent governor and companion
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ بْنُ سَهْلٍ: Al-Fadl ibn Sahl, a key Abbasid official

ai.seo_question: What did Ar-Rayyan ibn al-Salt request from Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) and how did the Imam respond?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Imam’s *‘ilm al-ghayb* (knowledge of the unseen) through his precise anticipation of Rayyan ibn al-Salt’s specific desires for clothing and dirhams minted with his name. It serves as a key indicator of divine leadership (*Imamah*) during the Abbasid era, demonstrating the Imam’s authority even when political power was held by figures like Al-Fadl ibn Sahl. The gift of coins bearing his name also subtly asserts his spiritual and temporal legitimacy amidst the ruling caliphs.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 47-10 Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Idris - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abil Khattab, on the authority of Mo’ammar ibn Khallad that Ar-Rayyan ibn al-Salt told him

in Marv where he had just been dispatched as governor to some of the towns of Khorasan by Al-Fadhl ibn Sahl, “I’d like you to seek permission for me to see Abil Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) and greet him (a.s.). I’d really wish that he (a.s.) would donate to me some of his own robes and give me some Dirham coins which have been issued in his own name.” I went in to see Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) and before I could say anything, the Imam (a.s.) said, “In fact, Ar-Ryan ibn al-Salt has sought permission to visit me, and has asked for some of my robes and Dirhams. I grant him permission to come in.” Then Ar-Ryan entered and greeted the Imam (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) granted him two sets of robes and thirty Dirhams which had been coined in his name.”
